_readme: How the launch is timed. Each rocket has a number of launch moments (times you must press a key at the right time) and a window tightness. window_tightness: 1.0 = normal. A bigger number means a TIGHTER window (harder to hit). A smaller number means a looser window (easier). A cheaper rocket has more moments and tighter windows. Every value has a source: a link, a written game-design choice, or PLACEHOLDER (made up for now; a student replaces it before the final submission). TIMED PRESS (the ring that closes on a target): base_speed 1.0 = the ring takes close_seconds to close; speed 2.0 closes twice as fast. The windows are a share of the ring's trip, so a faster ring gives less time to press. perfect_window and good_window are that share (0.06 = 6% of the trip, before and after the target). Bigger window_tightness makes both windows smaller. The levels do NOT change any of this: timing is the same for every character. LAUNCH: each rocket lists its moment_ids in order. Each moment has a miss_cost: a Miss costs fuel (percent lost) or damages a part (percent damaged). The cost is stored in GameState.damage and never ends the mission. Perfect or Good costs nothing. The Flight screen uses the damage: fuel = less fuel for the arrival burn, solar_panel = less power made, antenna = weaker signal, instruments = less data.

launch3d._readme: The 3D launch (UPGRADE_PLAN_V2 step 16), beat by beat. Times in seconds. countdown_from = the big numbers count down from here; countdown_step_seconds = time per number. climb_height = how high (in game meters) the rocket climbs before the view cuts to space; pitch_degrees = how far it tips over while climbing. prompt_speed = how fast the in-flight rings close (1 = the same as the ignition ring); rebalance_speed = the ENGINE OUT ring. hold_detumble_seconds = how long you must hold Space to stop the spin; start_spin_degrees = how fast the spacecraft spins after release (degrees per second). telemetry = the numbers on the tiles (display only).

telemetry.source: Display only (Upgrade step 16, 2026-11-14). NASA Glenn Rocket Principles: low Earth orbit needs more than 28,000 km/h, and escape from Earth about 40,250 km/h: https://www.grc.nasa.gov/www/k-12/rocket/TRCRocket/rocket_principles.html (the 200 km height is a game-design choice inside low Earth orbit).

structure_check._readme: Structure strength (the Hammering team score, 0-100) is checked after the launch presses (PLAN.md section 8). Below min_strength, the rocket's shaking loosens shake_part: it gets shake_damage_percent damage (like a launch Miss). The damage kinds are the same as miss_cost kinds.
